citation: Jayathissa et al. (2017). Optimising building net energy demand with dynamic BIPV shading. Applied Energy 202, 726–735.
description: The RC Building Simulator is a five-resistance, one-capacitance building model published by the Architecture and Building Systems group at ETH Zürich. Its Python workflow represents a zone, windows, energy supply and emission systems, then calculates heat and lighting demand from weather, solar gains, occupancy and internal gains. Outputs include heating and cooling demand, system electricity or fuel use and zone, surface and thermal-mass temperatures. Coverage is globally configurable for a chosen building, with the guide illustrating hourly simulation and an 8,760-hour annual loop. Public source is free under an amended MIT licence that additionally requires a research reference to the ETH group. A limitation is the reduced thermal representation and the age of the installation guidance; users must check dependencies and suitability for complex buildings. It can support rapid building-demand simulations, complementary to the more detailed EnergyPlus model (model-energyplus). The README cites the 2017 dynamic BIPV-shading study, and its wiki provides a complete first simulation. No weather file or building model was downloaded.
